html:
The Crimean War was fought from 1853 to 1856 between Russia and an alliance of the Ottoman Empire, Britain, France and, from 1855, the Kingdom of Sardinia. Most of the fighting was on the Crimean peninsula in the Black Sea.

It began over Russia's claim to protect Orthodox Christians in Ottoman lands and a quarrel over the holy places in Jerusalem. Behind that lay British and French fear that Russia would gain from Ottoman weakness and reach the Mediterranean. Russia occupied the Danube principalities in 1853 and sank an Ottoman fleet at Sinop. In 1854 the allies landed in Crimea and besieged the naval base of Sevastopol, which fell after eleven months in September 1855. Battles on the way included Balaclava, with its doomed Charge of the Light Brigade.

Disease killed far more soldiers than battle. Florence Nightingale reformed the British army hospital at Scutari, and the young Leo Tolstoy fought at Sevastopol and wrote about it. It was among the first wars covered by newspaper reporters, the telegraph and photographs.

The Treaty of Paris of 1856 barred warships from the Black Sea. Defeat pushed Russia's tsar Alexander II into reforms, above all the emancipation of the serfs in 1861. The Ottomans began borrowing in Europe to pay for the war, a road that led to the Imperial Ottoman Bank and later the foreign control of their debts.
sum: The Crimean War was fought from 1853 to 1856 between Russia and an alliance of the Ottoman Empire, Britain, France and, from 1855, the Kingdom of Sardinia. Most of the fighting was on the Crimean peninsula in the Black Sea.
